Replace each `___` with code, remove `#| eval: false` and run the chunk.

**Question for today:** Can we build one tidy table from three wide tables?

```{r}
#| label: setup
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, here)
```

## 1. Three wide tables

Each table has one row per country and one column per year. Life expectancy also holds the continent.

```{r}
#| label: look
here("data", "income_wide.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  glimpse()
```

## 2. Keys

A key is the column (or columns) that identify a row. After reshaping, the key is `country` + `year`. A join matches rows by key.

`left_join()` keeps every row of the table on the left and adds the matching columns from the table on the right.

## 3. Reshape life expectancy

The first table is the left table. Reshape it as in class 8.

```{r}
#| label: reshape-life
#| eval: false
here("data", "life_expectancy_wide.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  pivot_longer(`1952`:`2007`, names_to = "year", values_to = "___",
               names_transform = as.integer)
```

## 4. Reshape income and join it

Reshape the income table inside `left_join()`. The key is `country` and `year`.

```{r}
#| label: join-income
#| eval: false
here("data", "life_expectancy_wide.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  pivot_longer(`1952`:`2007`, names_to = "year", values_to = "life_exp",
               names_transform = as.integer) |>
  left_join(
    here("data", "income_wide.csv") |>
      read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
      pivot_longer(`1952`:`2007`, names_to = "year", values_to = "___",
                   names_transform = as.integer),
    by = c("___", "year")
  )
```

## 5. Add population and save

Repeat the join for `population_wide.csv`, then save the result.

```{r}
#| label: join-all
#| eval: false
here("data", "life_expectancy_wide.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  pivot_longer(`1952`:`2007`, names_to = "year", values_to = "life_exp",
               names_transform = as.integer) |>
  left_join(
    here("data", "income_wide.csv") |>
      read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
      pivot_longer(`1952`:`2007`, names_to = "year", values_to = "income",
                   names_transform = as.integer),
    by = c("country", "year")
  ) |>
  left_join(
    here("data", "___.csv") |>
      read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
      pivot_longer(`1952`:`2007`, names_to = "year", values_to = "___",
                   names_transform = as.integer),
    by = c("country", "year")
  ) |>
  write_csv(here("data", "rosling_tidy.csv"))
```

## 6. Check the row count and missing values

Life expectancy has 142 countries and 12 years, so the table must have 1,704 rows. More rows mean a repeated key. Fewer rows mean a join dropped rows. See the [data quality checklist](../../capstone/data_quality_checklist.md).

```{r}
#| label: check
#| eval: false
here("data", "rosling_tidy.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  summarize(rows = ___, countries = n_distinct(country), missing = sum(is.na(income)))
```
